items.title: Urban greenspace exposure and inequality link to mortality
items.one_liner: Research across multiple countries shows urban greenspace exposure and inequality are associated with mortality in cities.
items.why: Links directly to environmental justice, access to urban nature, and human health benefits of ecosystem services.
items.action: Review the multi-country methodology to evaluate health impacts of greenspace access in Kabul.

items.title: Brazilian Cities Accelerate Urban Climate Action from COP30
items.one_liner: Brazilian cities are advancing local climate action as the COP30 implementation legacy consolidates.
items.why: Offers a Global South case study on translating international climate agreements into local urban plans.
items.action: Compare municipal implementation frameworks between Brazilian cities and Kabul.

items.title: Gujarat Urban Greening Policy Sets 20% Green Cover Target
items.one_liner: Gujarat's new urban greening policy sets a mandatory target of 20% green cover for urban areas.
items.why: Provides a policy benchmark for green-blue infrastructure targets in semi-arid Global South urban settings.
items.action: Examine policy implementation mechanisms for application in data-scarce urban environments.

items.title: Climate Adaptation Funding Is Falling Behind
items.one_liner: Reports indicate that global climate adaptation funding is falling far behind required levels.
items.why: Contextualizes financial constraints for urban ecosystem-based adaptation and planning in the Global South.
items.action: Investigate adaptation funding shortfalls affecting developing regions like Afghanistan.

items.title: CREAF Research on Urban Trees at Smart City Expo 2026
items.one_liner: CREAF showcased research on urban trees and their ecosystem functions at Smart City Expo 2026.
items.why: Highlights advanced methods for studying urban cooling and heat mitigation via urban forestry.
items.action: Look up CREAF's presented models for potential use in spatial cooling analyses.

items.title: UNEP Warns Climate Adaptation Finance Remains Below Needs
items.one_liner: UNEP warns that climate adaptation financing is far below developing countries' actual requirements.
items.why: Provides authoritative figures on the adaptation gap facing developing nations and vulnerable cities.
items.action: Incorporate UNEP financing gap data into the background justification for Kabul planning.

items.title: Punjab Plans GBP300,000 Climate-Resilient Farming Project
items.one_liner: Punjab plans a GBP300,000 project focused on climate-resilient farming for Cholistan and Thal.
items.why: Relates to peri-urban agriculture and climate resilience in semi-arid South Asian settings.
items.action: Review project design details for peri-urban agricultural adaptation approaches.

items.title: COP31 in Turkey: What to Expect at the 2026 UN Climate Summit
items.one_liner: Previews outline expectations and agendas for the upcoming 2026 UN Climate Summit (COP31) in Turkey.
items.why: Informs international policy frameworks relevant to climate adaptation and urban resilience strategies.
items.action: Monitor COP31 urban agenda discussions relating to semi-arid regions.

items.title: UN Warns Climate Adaptation Finance Falls Short in Africa
items.one_liner: The UN warns of severe adaptation funding shortages as developing regions face escalating climate costs.
items.why: Reinforces the challenge of securing resources for urban environmental planning in resource-constrained contexts.
items.action: Check regional cost estimates to understand economic barriers in fragile states.
